back.body: FOUR NATIONAL LEVELS, each containing the one below · EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONDER: first on scene, basic life support, minimal kit · EMT: the backbone — assessment · airway · oxygen · ventilation · bleeding · splinting · childbirth · a short mostly-assisted medication list · ADVANCED EMT: adds some advanced airways, IV access, wider medication list · PARAMEDIC: widest — advanced airways, cardiac monitoring and interpretation, large medication list · THE LEVEL IS WHAT THEY ARE TRAINED AND LICENSED TO DO — not the vehicle, not the patch · YOUR STATE SETS YOUR SCOPE and it may be narrower · THE POINT: recognise when you need the level above you, AND CALL EARLY
back.why_it_matters: Eighteen minutes is eighteen minutes whether you ask at minute four or minute twenty.

front.title: EMS systems and medical direction
front.summary: The protocol IS the doctor's instruction

back.body: AN EMS SYSTEM IS A CHAIN, not a fleet: ACCESS → DISPATCH → FIRST RESPONSE → TRANSPORT → HOSPITAL → REHABILITATION · behind it: training, licensing, equipment, communications, funding · around it: QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, which changes what needs changing · It is only as good as its worst handover · YOU DO NOT PRACTISE ON YOUR OWN LICENCE — you practise under a PHYSICIAN MEDICAL DIRECTOR'S, delegated · OFFLINE = protocols and standing orders WRITTEN IN ADVANCE, covering most of what you do · ONLINE = a physician in REAL TIME · THE PROTOCOL IS THE DEFAULT ANSWER; THE CALL IS FOR WHAT IT DID NOT ANTICIPATE — and is not skipped when protocol says to make it
back.why_it_matters: He stood holding the mask asking whether to phone the doctor who had signed the order eighteen months earlier.

front.title: Roles and professionalism
front.summary: Yourself first, so the arithmetic works

back.body: PRIORITY ORDER: YOURSELF → CREW → PATIENT → BYSTANDERS · not callousness — AN INJURED EMT BECOMES A SECOND PATIENT and the ambulance coming for the first is now needed twice · CORE ROLE: assess · treat IN SCOPE · transport safely to the RIGHT place · hand over accurately with a record that matches · PROFESSIONALISM IS NOT UNIFORM — it is punctuality, confidentiality, how you speak to frightened people, and HOW YOU TALK ABOUT PATIENTS WHEN THEY CANNOT HEAR YOU · ADVOCACY only counts when it costs something: the paramedic that delays you, the trauma centre that is further · CONTINUING EDUCATION — out-of-date practice feels exactly as confident as current practice · They will remember whether you were kind
back.why_it_matters: He crossed a live carriageway because it felt unthinkable not to, and she waited longer for it.

back.body: QI = the system looking at WHAT IT ACTUALLY DID and changing what needs changing · IT RUNS ON YOUR PATIENT CARE REPORTS — a vague record makes the whole process BLIND, at a scale of thousands of calls · SYSTEMS RATHER THAN BLAME: ask what made the error POSSIBLE, not who made it — a process that catches a careful person at 4am will catch the next one · BLAME STOPS REPORTING, AND A SYSTEM WITH NO REPORTS CANNOT IMPROVE · EVIDENCE-BASED = used because it is SHOWN to work, not because it is traditional · ALREADY REVERSED: routine BACKBOARDING · universal HIGH-FLOW OXYGEN · TOURNIQUETS as a last resort · 'We have always done it this way' is a DESCRIPTION, not a justification · A PATIENT IMPROVING DOES NOT PROVE YOU HELPED — most patients improve
back.why_it_matters: Thousands of boarded patients doing well is what happens either way. That is why it took evidence.

back.body: EMS GOES WHERE NOTHING ELSE IN HEALTHCARE GOES — into homes, at night, unannounced · PREVENTION: car seats · smoke alarms · the rug at the top of the stairs · helmets — unglamorous, and it prevents more harm over a career than any single call · DATA: one call is a photograph, ten thousand are a MAP — the junction, the building, the postcode — but only if the reports were written well enough to see it · CREWS SEE EMERGING PROBLEMS FIRST — a new drug shows up in ambulances before anywhere official · FREQUENT CALLERS SIGNAL UNMET NEED, NOT MISUSE — answer with a REFERRAL, not a sigh; know what pathways your service has · SAFEGUARDING sits here: you may be the only professional who sees the house
back.why_it_matters: Nothing about her had been a misuse of anything. It had been a question nobody had answered.

front.title: Standard precautions and PPE
front.summary: Dress for the task, not the call

back.body: UNIVERSAL, BECAUSE YOU CANNOT TELL BY LOOKING — most carriers do not know themselves · GLOVES FOR EVERY PATIENT CONTACT · EYE PROTECTION + GOWN wherever splashing is FORESEEABLE: suctioning · childbirth · vomiting · arterial bleeding · agitation — AND PUT THEM ON BEFORE YOU START · MASK ON THE PATIENT = SOURCE CONTROL, protects everyone else · mask on you = personal protection · AIRBORNE: your service's respirator policy, including FIT TESTING · CHOOSE PPE FROM THE TASK, NOT THE DISPATCH CODE — dispatch is frequently wrong · HAND HYGIENE IS THE MOST EFFECTIVE SINGLE MEASURE and the most skipped — gloves are NOT a substitute · MOST CONTAMINATION HAPPENS DURING REMOVAL
back.why_it_matters: The call was chest pain. What they were about to do was lean over his face.

back.body: FOUR ROUTES: BLOODBORNE · AIRBORNE · DROPLET · CONTACT (including surfaces) · BLOODBORNE NEEDS A ROUTE IN: needlestick · splash to eyes/nose/mouth · blood into BROKEN skin — INTACT SKIN IS AN EXCELLENT BARRIER · AIRBORNE stays suspended and travels; DROPLETS fall fast over a short distance · CONTACT is the underestimated one — rails, cables, handles · SHARPS ARE THE HIGHEST-RISK EXPOSURE, and MOST HAPPEN AFTER THE PROCEDURE, DURING TIDYING UP, to someone who did not use the needle · NEVER RECAP · dispose YOURSELF, IMMEDIATELY · never put one down · EXPOSED? WASH OR IRRIGATE, THEN REPORT IMMEDIATELY — treatment is TIME-CRITICAL, so delay REMOVES the option · Report everything, however small
back.why_it_matters: Nobody has ever been criticised for reporting an exposure too quickly.

front.title: Scene safety
front.summary: A weather report, not a door

back.body: SCENE SAFETY IS CONTINUOUS — dispatch to back in the vehicle, NOT a check on arrival · A SAFE SCENE CAN STOP BEING SAFE WHILE YOU WORK · BEFORE ARRIVAL: dispatch detail · address history · what you can hear · A SCENE THAT GOES QUIET AS YOU ARRIVE IS TELLING YOU SOMETHING · AT THE DOORWAY, three seconds: HOW MANY PEOPLE · WHERE ARE THE EXITS · WHAT IS IN REACH · VIOLENCE, WEAPONS OR UNSECURED = STAGE AND WAIT FOR POLICE, whatever dispatch says about bleeding · NEVER GET CORNERED — keep your route out clear, and do not block THEIRS · HAZARDS: traffic · unstable vehicles · fire · electricity · animals · sharps · structures · PARK to protect the area and to leave FORWARDS · IF IT TURNS UNSAFE, LEAVE — whatever stage you are at
back.why_it_matters: Four minutes waiting for police is a cost. Not going out at all has a different price.

back.body: STRESS IS THE PREDICTABLE RESULT OF THE JOB, not a fault in you · ACUTE: during or just after an incident — obvious cause, usually settles · CUMULATIVE: builds over MONTHS AND YEARS out of ordinary calls with NO MOMENT TO POINT AT — which is why it is the dangerous one and why nobody notices it starting · SIGNS: sleep · irritability · WITHDRAWAL · loss of interest · drinking more · intrusive memories · feeling nothing · SOME CALLS LAND HARD REGARDLESS OF EXPERIENCE: children · people you know · mass casualties · CALLS THAT RESEMBLE YOUR OWN LIFE · TALKING IS PROFESSIONAL BEHAVIOUR · FIND YOUR SUPPORT ROUTES BEFORE YOU NEED THEM · WATCH YOUR CREWMATE — asking twice is often the whole intervention
back.why_it_matters: Nothing had happened to him. That was the point — nothing had happened, a hundred times, over four years.

back.body: BACKS END MORE EMS CAREERS THAN ANY DRAMATIC EVENT — and almost all of it is CUMULATIVE, hundreds of lifts that did not hurt at the time · KEEP THE WEIGHT CLOSE — distance MULTIPLIES the force through your spine; close and at arm's length are two different weights · LIFT WITH YOUR LEGS · natural curve in the back · feet apart · head up · NEVER TWIST UNDER LOAD — MOVE YOUR FEET; it is the movement most associated with injury and the easiest to do without noticing · PUSH rather than PULL · set the HEIGHT so nobody stoops · SAY YOUR LIMIT BEFORE THE LIFT, not halfway up the stairs · CALL AN ASSIST — eight minutes against a career · USE THE EQUIPMENT · BRIEF THE LIFT: who calls it, what the count is, where it goes
back.why_it_matters: The lift was textbook. It was the six inches at the end, turning his shoulders instead of his feet.

back.body: See the skill card steps. Critical: BRIEF IT FIRST (who calls it, the count, the route), state your limits NOW, call an assist if unsure, GET CLOSE before you lift, stable base and natural curve, LIFT WITH THE LEGS, NEVER TWIST UNDER LOAD — move your feet, and lower with the same technique because injuries happen on the way down too.
back.why_it_matters: Most bad lifts go wrong because two people moved at different moments.

back.body: FATIGUE DEGRADES JUDGEMENT AND REACTION TIME WHILE LEAVING CONFIDENCE INTACT — a tired clinician feels like themselves · NIGHTS ARE PHYSIOLOGICALLY HARD however many you have done — 'adapted' usually means tolerating impairment, not avoiding it · SLEEP DEBT ACCUMULATES and is NOT cleared by one lie-in · HELPS: strategic naps · DEFEND daytime sleep (blackout, phone off, household warned) · CAFFEINE LATE IN A SHIFT IS BORROWED FROM THE SLEEP AFTER IT · THE DRIVE HOME AFTER NIGHTS IS ONE OF THE HIGHEST-RISK THINGS YOU DO ALL WEEK — too tired? Do not drive · EAT: blood sugar swings hit concentration and patience · FITNESS FOR DUTY ALSO MEANS illness, medication, and personal circumstances — SAYING SO IS A PROFESSIONAL ACT
back.why_it_matters: The most dangerous part of that week was never going to be a patient.

back.body: SCOPE OF PRACTICE = WHAT YOU MAY DO — set by the STATE, narrowed by your MEDICAL DIRECTOR and your PROTOCOLS · STANDARD OF CARE = HOW WELL YOU MUST DO IT · THE TEST: what a REASONABLE, PRUDENT EMT of SIMILAR TRAINING would do in SIMILAR CIRCUMSTANCES · NOT perfection · NOT measured against paramedics or physicians · NOT judged with HINDSIGHT — on what you knew AT THE TIME · Defined by protocols, guidelines, accepted practice and training · ACTING OUTSIDE SCOPE IS A BREACH EVEN WHEN IT WORKS — a good outcome is an outcome, not authority · DOING LESS THAN SCOPE ALLOWS CAN ALSO BREACH THE STANDARD — under-treating is not the safe direction · LAW asks what you MAY; ETHICS asks what you SHOULD
back.why_it_matters: A good outcome is an outcome. It is not authority.

front.title: Consent
front.summary: A running conversation, not a signature

back.body: CONSENT IS NEEDED BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANYBODY, and it must be INFORMED: they understand WHAT you propose · WHY · the RISKS · what happens IF THEY DECLINE — a nod is not necessarily any of that · EXPRESSED: given directly, spoken or by clear gesture · IMPLIED: cannot consent AND an emergency — covers only what the emergency requires · MINORS: parent or guardian, with exceptions (emancipated minors and jurisdiction-specific categories) — BUT IN A REAL EMERGENCY WITH NO GUARDIAN REACHABLE, IMPLIED CONSENT APPLIES, SO DO NOT WAIT · INVOLUNTARY: under legal authority for danger to self or others — needs LAW ENFORCEMENT or a designated official, almost never an EMT alone · CONSENT FOR ONE THING IS NOT CONSENT FOR EVERYTHING
back.why_it_matters: Implied consent exists so nobody stands over a deteriorating child waiting for a phone to be answered.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-01-03-02. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: E — EXPRESSED: spoken, written, or an unmistakable gesture · I — IMPLIED: cannot consent + an emergency; the law assumes a reasonable person would want care · M — MINORS: parent or guardian, with exceptions; A REAL EMERGENCY WITH NO GUARDIAN REACHABLE FALLS BACK TO IMPLIED · I — INVOLUNTARY: under legal authority for danger to self or others, needing law enforcement or a designated official · INFORMED = what, why, the risks, and what happens if they say no
back.why_it_matters: The two I's sit at either end and are opposites: one assumes they would say yes, the other overrides them saying no.

front.title: Refusal of care
front.summary: The glucose meter before the form

back.body: A COMPETENT ADULT MAY REFUSE ANYTHING, including life-saving care, and your disagreement does not matter · BUT EVERYTHING RESTS ON 'COMPETENT' · CAPACITY = UNDERSTAND · RETAIN · WEIGH · COMMUNICATE, about THIS decision, NOW · CHECK WHAT MIGHT HAVE TAKEN IT AWAY: GLUCOSE · SATURATION · head injury · intoxication · infection · A REFUSAL WITHOUT CAPACITY IS NOT A REFUSAL · INFORMED MEANS PLAIN WORDS — say what could actually happen, including dying tonight · PERSUADE, more than once, differently · family · MEDICAL DIRECTION where protocol says · SAY OUT LOUD 'call us straight back if anything changes' AND MEAN IT · DOCUMENT: capacity and its basis · vitals + glucose · what you told them · THEIR WORDS IN QUOTES · witnesses · the advice to call back · REFUSALS ARE THE HIGHEST-RISK THING YOU DO ROUTINELY
back.why_it_matters: He was talking and adamant and his sugar was 2.5. The refusal had never been a decision.

back.body: See the skill card steps. Critical: assess as much as they allow, CHECK GLUCOSE AND SATURATION FIRST, full vitals, look for capacity-impairing causes, ASSESS CAPACITY (understand/retain/weigh/communicate), explain risks IN PLAIN WORDS, persuade more than once, medical direction where required, TELL THEM TO CALL BACK AND MEAN IT, signatures, and DOCUMENT EVERYTHING INCLUDING THEIR OWN WORDS.
back.why_it_matters: The documentation is the entire defence, and the process behind it is what stops it being needed.

back.body: NEGLIGENCE NEEDS ALL FOUR ELEMENTS — remove one and there is none · DUTY: an obligation to act — on duty and dispatched, you have one · DERELICTION: breached the standard, by doing something wrong OR failing to do something · DIRECT CAUSE: the breach actually caused the harm, not coincidentally · DAMAGES: real harm — physical, psychological or financial · CAUSATION IS WHERE MANY CLAIMS FAIL: a mistake that harmed nobody is a MISTAKE, not negligence · ABANDONMENT = ending care WITHOUT CONSENT and WITHOUT handing over to EQUAL OR HIGHER TRAINING · IT HAPPENS AT HOSPITAL MORE OFTEN THAN ON SCENE — a corridor trolley with no handover is abandonment, however full the department · A receptionist or porter is NOT a handover · Duty starts when care starts
back.why_it_matters: A building full of doctors and nurses, not one of whom had accepted her from them.

back.body: D — DUTY: an obligation to act · D — DERELICTION: breached the standard of care, by commission OR omission · D — DIRECT CAUSE: the breach actually caused the harm · D — DAMAGES: real harm resulted · ALL FOUR OR NONE — an error that harmed nobody has no causation and no damages; a bad outcome after correct care has damages but no breach
back.why_it_matters: A four-legged stool. Take away any leg and it is just some wood on the floor.

front.title: Confidentiality
front.summary: The careers end on social media

back.body: EVERYTHING you learn is CONFIDENTIAL — condition, history, address, the state of the house, what they said · SHARE ONLY WITH A LEGITIMATE NEED TO KNOW: clinical handover · your documentation · quality improvement · LEGALLY REQUIRED reporting · FAMILY ARE NOT AUTOMATICALLY ENTITLED — where the patient can say, ASK THEM · THE REAL BREACHES ARE CASUAL: corridors · lifts · queues · canteens — towns and hospitals are smaller than they feel · DO NOT POST ABOUT CALLS — not de-identified, not in a private group, not years later; a DATE, an AGE, a MECHANISM and a TOWN is a name to anyone who knows them · NO PHOTOGRAPHS ON A PERSONAL PHONE, shown or not · VISIBLE SCREENS AND CLIPBOARDS are the same breach · One of the commonest ways EMS careers end
back.why_it_matters: No name, no address. It had the date, the age, the mechanism and the town. His sister recognised it in four hours.

front.title: Advance directives and DNR
front.summary: A DNR is not 'do not treat'

back.body: AN ADVANCE DIRECTIVE = the patient speaking in advance for when they cannot · DNR = DO NOT ATTEMPT RESUSCITATION IF THE HEART OR BREATHING STOPS · IT IS NOT 'DO NOT TREAT' — THEY STILL GET pain relief in scope · oxygen · suction · positioning · warmth · conversation · transport · family support · Under-treating a DNR patient is a FAILURE OF CARE, not respect for wishes · POLST covers MORE: resuscitation, intubation, hospitalisation, antibiotics, feeding · VALIDITY RULES DIFFER BY JURISDICTION — learn yours BEFORE the bedroom floor at 4am · DOUBT, OR NO DOCUMENT? BEGIN RESUSCITATION — you can stop, you cannot undo not starting · A relative saying there is one somewhere is not a document · FAMILY DISTRESS DOES NOT OVERRIDE A VALID DIRECTIVE · Conflict? MEDICAL DIRECTION
back.why_it_matters: The form said do not attempt resuscitation. It had never said anything about the four hours in front of them.

back.body: SOME THINGS MUST BE REPORTED BY LAW whatever the patient wants — categories VARY, learn yours · COMMONLY: suspected CHILD abuse or neglect · ELDER or vulnerable adult abuse · GUNSHOT and STAB wounds · notifiable diseases · THE THRESHOLD IS SUSPICION, NOT PROOF — you are NOT investigating and being wrong costs you nothing · Report through your service's route and DOCUMENT IT · CRIME SCENES: PATIENT CARE COMES FIRST, always — no evidence outweighs a living patient · Then: ONE ROUTE IN AND OUT · touch only what you must · do not tidy · CUT AROUND HOLES IN CLOTHING, NEVER THROUGH — the defect is evidence and going round takes no longer · KEEP the clothing, PAPER not plastic, give it to POLICE · TELL THE OFFICER what you moved, touched, cut and where you walked
back.why_it_matters: He said it was the most useful thing anybody had said to him all night.

back.body: GOOD SAMARITAN LAWS protect VOLUNTARY help given IN GOOD FAITH WITHOUT EXPECTATION OF PAYMENT · Generally require: good faith · WITHIN YOUR TRAINING · no GROSS NEGLIGENCE or wilful misconduct · THEY DO NOT COVER RECKLESSNESS or acts far outside training — a shield for the person who stopped, not a licence for the person who improvised · WHETHER THEY APPLY ON DUTY VARIES and frequently they do NOT — on duty you already have a duty and other coverage · WHETHER YOU HAVE A DUTY TO ACT OFF DUTY ALSO VARIES — some jurisdictions impose one, most do not · CONSISTENT ALMOST EVERYWHERE: ONCE YOU BEGIN HELPING YOU HAVE ASSUMED A DUTY and cannot walk away · KNOW YOUR OWN STATE'S PROVISIONS
back.why_it_matters: Not stopping is a question about duty. Starting and then leaving is a different question entirely.
